newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Qatar emir to switch his hold on income to state.
newsitem.headline: Qatar emir to switch his hold on income to state.

text.p: Qatar plans to switch control over its revenues to the state from the oil-rich country's ruler, the emir said in remarks published on Saturday.

"Qatar is studying a draft law to keep state funds owned by the state not privately owned by a person or almost a private holding of the head of state," Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani told Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam daily.
Diplomats and bankers say former emir Sheikh Khalifa held on to between three and seven billion dollars of Qatari funds abroad when he was toppled in June 1995 by his son Sheikh Hamad.
The two have held reconciliation talks in recent months in an attempt to gain control over at least part of the funds.

Qatar, one of the highest gross national products per capita in the world, is a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and also controls the world's third largest natural gas reserves after Russia and Iran.
